name: ditaa
desc: Convert ASCII diagrams into proper bitmap graphics
why: Turns ASCII box-and-line drawings into bitmap diagrams, a clean transform from text shapes into pixels.

brief.what_it_is: ditaa is a small command-line utility written in Java that converts ASCII-art diagrams (drawings made of characters like | / - +) into bitmap images. It reads a text file containing the diagram and writes out a rendered image, PNG by default. It can also process HTML files, replacing the contents of pre class='textdiagram' blocks with generated tags. The homepage describes the project as open source under the GPL.
brief.why_it_exists: The author, Stathis Sideris, gives several reasons: hack value ('I wanted to know if/how it could be done and how easily'), modernising old ASCII diagrams in legacy FAQs, embedding diagrams in text-based formats like HTML, DocBook, LaTeX and code comments, and keeping diagrams as editable text that can be re-rendered by newer versions.
brief.how_it_works: ditaa interprets the ASCII drawing as a series of open and closed shapes, then renders those shapes as graphics. Extra markup extends what it can draw: colour codes (cXXX hex or named codes like cRED), tags such as {d}, {s} and {io} for special symbols, dashed lines when a line contains = or :, round corners when / and \ join corners, and a * point marker. Colour applies only inside closed shapes, and text inside dark fills is switched to white.

Starts ditaa from the command line, where XXX is the version number; running it with no arguments prints the options help.

brief.install_notes: The homepage says you need a recent Java runtime (JRE) to run ditaa. Java 1.5 or higher gives the best anti-aliasing. Downloads are on the SourceForge project page, and the source can be checked out with svn. No account or other configuration is mentioned. Homebrew's own caveats are empty.
brief.standout: Rather than parsing a separate diagram language, ditaa treats the ASCII drawing itself as the source, so the same text file can be re-rendered later with a newer version and look better with no edits. Its rules are loose: dashed lines spread from one = or : character, and corners join with / and \ to make rounded shapes.
brief.status: Unknown. The homepage has no release date or last-commit date. It still points to SourceForge and Subversion, and it mentions old versions (0.6b and 0.8). The 'Text handling' section is marked 'still being written' and point markers are called 'experimental'. I did not check the SourceForge project page or the Homebrew formula.
brief.caveats: Requires Java, so it runs wherever a JRE does. The homepage is undated and partly out of date: it refers to SVN on SourceForge and to versions 0.6b and 0.8. Some features are marked experimental or unfinished (point markers, the text handling section, and the tag list is described as only 'some for now' for colour names). The author notes that not every old ASCII diagram will convert cleanly because drawing styles differ. The homepage does not mention a licence version beyond 'GPL'.
quotes: ditaa is a small command-line utility written in Java, that can convert diagrams drawn using ascii art
ditaa is a diagram markup language, with very loose syntax.
Simply for hack value. I wanted to know if/how it could be done and how easily.
